tagline: Providing safe, reliable, and affordable utility services and renewable energy in a sustainable way to better the lives of the communities we serve.
hero_kpi_rationale: NWN is a utility company (natural gas and water) that is investing heavily in its critical infrastructure. Capital expenditures of 466.9 million USD in 2025 reflect continued commitment to safety, reliability, and network expansion, including the strategic acquisition of SiEnergy in Texas.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: The difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, representing profitability before other expenses.
kpis.description: Measures the direct profitability of services provided by the company.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue, showing operational efficiency.
kpis.description: Indicates operating performance before interest and taxes.
kpis.signal: Reflects the ability to generate profits from core business activities.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Amount invested in physical assets to maintain or expand operations.
kpis.description: Represents spending on critical utility infrastructure, including acquisitions.
kpis.signal: Significant investment in infrastructure for safety and reliability.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by utility services, inherently recurring and stable.
kpis.description: Utility revenues are inherently recurring due to constant demand and regulated rates.
kpis.signal: Revenue stability through the regulated nature of utility services.

kpis.name: Employees
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: The number of employees is an indicator of organization size and operational needs.
kpis.signal: Indicator of size and operational capacity.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net revenue after all expenses, interest, and taxes, reflecting overall profitability.
kpis.description: NW Holdings consolidated net income for 2025, up 34.4 million USD from 2024.
kpis.signal: Significant net income growth driven by new rates and SiEnergy acquisition.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 6.17 billion EUR in the most recent year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 2.68 billion EUR in the most recent year

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: 43.6% increase in consolidated net income, reflecting strength of operations and positive impact of SiEnergy acquisition.
kpis.description: NW Holdings recorded net income increase of 34.4 million USD, primarily attributable to new rates approved by the Oregon Public Utilities Commission, effective November 2024 and October 2025, as well as the SiEnergy acquisition in January 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant growth driven by new Oregon rates and SiEnergy integration.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Regulatory Risk on Cost Recovery
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central to the 10-K, mentioned early with strong language ('adversely impact', 'failure to approve rates'). It concerns the ability to recover investment and operating costs through rates, fundamental for regulated utilities. The Regulation category carries high weight in the sector. The text emphasizes approval delays, judicial appeals, and legislative restrictions (e.g., HB 3179), aggravating the risk.

risks.title: Legislative Restrictions on Rate Filings
risks.score_rationale: The factor is specifically tied to Oregon law HB 3179, cited with precision. The language expresses concern ('inability to file', 'delay recovery'). This risk is new or heightened compared to the prior year due to recent legislation. The Regulation category is critical for utilities. The risk limits rate flexibility for 18 months, impacting cash flow.

risks.title: Potential Loss of Regulatory Accounting Treatment
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as an existential risk: loss of regulatory assets and inability to defer costs. The language is strong ('required to write off', 'precluded from future deferral'). This risk is stable but critical as it calls into question the entire accounting model for regulated operations. The Regulation category is highly weighted.

risks.title: Acquisition Integration and Performance
risks.score_rationale: The risk is highlighted with concrete examples (SiEnergy acquisition in 2025). The language is repetitive and detailed ('unexpected costs', 'fail to achieve benefits', 'undisclosed liabilities'). Multiple recent acquisitions increase exposure. While the Strategy category is less weighted than Regulation, the intensity of language and recent context justify high severity.

risks.title: Pressure on Natural Gas Public Perception
risks.score_rationale: The risk is described in detail with specific threats: opposition from advocacy groups, health and climate concerns, methane leaks. The language is alarming ('opposed altogether', 'detrimental health effects'). The risk is increasing due to growing activism. Reputation deterioration could impact regulatory decisions and customer growth.

risks.title: Increased Regulatory Complexity from Expansion
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes entry into new states (Texas, Idaho, Arizona) and regulation by new authorities (e.g., Railroad Commission of Texas). The language indicates heightened risk of unintentional non-compliance. While the risk is tied to growth, it is firmly rooted in the Regulation category, which is critical. The context of recent external growth (SiEnergy, Pines) reinforces this risk.

risks.title: Risks Related to Tax Changes and Interpretations
risks.score_rationale: The tax risk is well-described, with references to audits, litigation, and uncertainty over deferred assets. The language is cautious ('cannot predict', 'adverse judgments'). While amounts at stake could be material, the risk is less central than regulatory risks. The Capital category is moderately weighted. The risk is stable, with no mention of major recent changes.

ai_positioning.summary: NWN does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its report.
